Meeting title: Model Catalog Demo - Sunrise Clinic
Attendees: Rebecca Lin (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortiz (Redwood SE), Elena Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Sharma (CTO, Sunrise), Jordan Lee (Platform Engineer), Maya Patel (Head of Data), Evan Kim (Security)

topics: Selecting open models (Llama 3, Mistral, Falcon variants)
Benchmark results and interpretation (latency, cost, quality)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Rebecca Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Rebecca from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We've got Marcus and Elena from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Sharma: Hi, good thanks.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Afternoon, thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Marcus Ortiz: Hi all, Marcus here. Today we'll run through the model catalog, show you how we select open models, go over benchmark numbers, and examine the compatibility matrix so you can see what runs where and why.
[00:25] Maya Patel: Great, we're especially interested in open models and how they behave on different hardware. Cost and latency are both super important.
[00:32] Elena Park: Totally. We'll start with the catalog UI in the Console, then jump into the Optimize suggestions for quantization profiles and batching, and finally show how the compatibility matrix maps models to runtimes and instance types.
[00:45] Marcus Ortiz: Quick qualification — what's your timeline for a pilot? And do you expect any PHI in the prompts during the pilot?
[00:52] Dr. Priya Sharma: We're hoping for a pilot in May, ideally early May. We'll use de-identified but sensitive clinical notes to start, so data handling is a big concern.
[00:59] Evan Kim: From security, we need SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, and SAML SSO. Also we have strict data residency rules for certain states.
[01:10] Rebecca Lin: Understood. We'll make sure the security pack includes all of that. We can run the pilot on our Private offering if needed for residency or on Dedicated if you want predictable throughput.
[01:22] Marcus Ortiz: Ok jumping into the Console — here's the Model Catalog page. You'll see we categorize models by family and by verified performance profiles. For open models we have Llama 3 8B, Llama 3 70B, Mistral Large, Mistral Mix, Falcon-40B, and a few smaller LLMs for code and embeddings.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: Quick question — are the Llama variants run in open-source weights or via a licensed bundle?
[01:50] Elena Park: We support both—if you bring weights you can host privately; we also serve curated open checkpoints when licensing permits. For the catalog we show the performance profile against our test corpus.
[01:59] Marcus Ortiz: Here's a benchmark row: latency p50, p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. Note that these numbers are measured on our standard 8xA100 profile unless noted otherwise.
[02:12] Maya Patel: I see Mistral has much better cost per token at 2k context compared to Llama 3, is that typical?
[02:18] Marcus Ortiz: Yes — model architecture and quantization friendliness matter. Mistral tends to be lighter and runs faster at similar quality for many tasks. Llama 3 70B is higher quality on some reasoning tasks but costs more and has higher memory needs.
[02:30] [02:30] (minor crosstalk)
[02:35] Rebecca Lin: This is where the compatibility matrix is useful — it tells you which quantization profiles are supported per model and which hardware is compatible. For example, Llama 3 70B has two recommended quant profiles: q8_0 and q4_1 for inference. q4_1 gives big cost savings but can sometimes slightly degrade QA-style outputs.
[02:55] Jordan Lee: How do you validate quality regressions when we quantize?
[03:00] Elena Park: We tie Optimize to a set of eval prompts — you upload a prompt set and expected outputs, and Redwood runs daily regression checks. You can define thresholds (e.g., F1 drop <2%). If quantization triggers regressions, we flag it and recommend a different profile.
[03:15] Maya Patel: That sounds good. We'll want to use a baseline of our clinical Q&A prompts.
[03:20] Marcus Ortiz: Absolutely — if you share a small sample we'll run a head-to-head Llama 3 70B (q8_0), Mistral Mix (q4_1), and Falcon-40B on your prompts and show both latency and answer overlap metrics.
[03:33] Dr. Priya Sharma: On the private vs dedicated question — do we need to manage our own infra for Private?
[03:38] Rebecca Lin: Private deployments can be VPC-hosted with a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem bundles. For Dedicated, Redwood manages the GPU pool but isolates compute for you with reserved capacity. Private gives you full network control and is typical when you want air-gapped or strict residency.
[03:53] Evan Kim: For our compliance team, seeing audit logs and KMS integration is critical. Are audit logs available in the Console?
[03:59] Elena Park: Yes — Console exposes per-request logs, token-level cost breakdowns, and an audit stream that can be forwarded to your SIEM. KMS/HSM integrations are supported across Private and Dedicated, and hosted with customer-managed keys is available in some regions.
[04:15] [04:15] Marcus Ortiz: Moving on to the bench spreadsheet — here's a filtered view for 2k context with batch size 1. We show per-token latency, throughput, and end-to-end cost at different concurrency levels. Notice how batching improves throughput but increases p95 latency.
[04:30] Jordan Lee: Do you have numbers for 512 vs 2k contexts? A lot of our user flows are short form.
[04:35] Marcus Ortiz: Yes, in the sheet we break out context lengths. Shorter contexts often benefit more from prefix caching and have lower memory footprint so you can pack more concurrent requests. For example, Mistral at 512 hits about 1.8x tokens/sec compared to 2k.
[04:48] Maya Patel: How do you recommend we pick the model? Is there a decision tree?
[04:52] Elena Park: We have a simple flow: accuracy requirement -> latency SLO -> cost constraint -> deployment constraints. If accuracy is strict and budget is secondary, pick Llama 3 70B; if cost/throughput and good quality suffice, Mistral or Falcon variants. Then look at compatibility, quantization viability, and whether Dedicated/Private is needed.
[05:10] [05:10] Dr. Priya Sharma: Can you walk through an example decision for a triage assistant that needs sub-500ms p95 and must never send PHI to third parties?
[05:20] Marcus Ortiz: For sub-500ms p95 you'd likely do Dedicated with 2-4 A100s per model shard and optimize batching to keep p95 low, maybe pick a smaller parameter set like Mistral Mix or a quantized Llama 3 8B (q8_0). For never sending PHI off-site, Private is the fit: VPC or on-prem with customer KMS.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: What about model fallbacks — if we run out of capacity on a Dedicated pool can requests go to a hosted variant?
[05:46] Elena Park: Yes, smart routing allows policy-based fallback to compatible variants or hosted capacity. You can set cost vs latency priorities; Redwood will route according to those rules and keep a canary so you don't unexpectedly change model outputs.
[05:58] [06:00] Marcus Ortiz: Now we'll demo the compatibility matrix view — columns are model, supported runtimes, recommended quant profiles, memory footprint, and verified tasks. You can filter by runtime (e.g., Triton, ORT, Redwood runtime) and hardware (A100, H100, T4).
[06:20] Maya Patel: Are kernels auto-selected per runtime? We saw some models run better in ORT with fused kernels.
[06:25] Marcus Ortiz: Yes, the runtime will pick optimized kernels based on architecture and sequence length distribution. We also compile variants for specific hardware to use fused attention where available.
[06:34] Dr. Priya Sharma: On accuracy — do you publish the test corpus? Is it representative?
[06:38] Elena Park: We publish the benchmark harness and the seed prompts used for our public profiles. For sensitive domains we ask customers to provide a redacted prompt set for apples-to-apples comparison.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: How reproducible are the numbers? If we run the same model on our Dedicated pool, will numbers match the catalog?
[06:53] Marcus Ortiz: They should be close; differences come from infra generation and patch levels. We version our model builds and include the model commit and runtime build in the compatibility matrix so you can match the environment exactly.
[07:05] [07:05] (brief pause)
[07:10] Rebecca Lin: Let's look at Optimize — given your workload we might recommend q4_1 for Mistral with batching and prefix/KV caching enabled. Optimize can estimate cost savings and flag potential quality regressions.
[07:24] Maya Patel: Is Optimize automated or advisory? Can we set auto-deploy?
[07:28] Elena Park: It's advisory by default. You can set automatic rollouts if regression thresholds are met, but for clinical data we recommend manual review.
[07:36] Marcus Ortiz: Also note that caching is tricky with PHI; you can encrypt and control cache retention windows per route so cached prefixes don't violate retention.
[07:48] Evan Kim: We'll need details on encryption-at-rest for caches and access controls.
[07:52] Elena Park: We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:56] [08:00] Marcus Ortiz: Ok switching to a live perf demo — small heads-up, transcription may skip some numbers. I'm launching a short head-to-head: Llama 3 8B (q8_0) vs Mistral Mix (q4_1) at 512 context on 8xA100.
[08:15] (sound of screen-share switching)
[08:20] Marcus Ortiz: Starting run now, p50… p95… tokens/sec… Llama 3 8B p50 ~40ms, p95 ~120ms, tokens/sec ~350. Mistral Mix p50 ~28ms, p95 ~95ms, tokens/sec ~520. Cost per 1k tokens Llama roughly $0.10, Mistral $0.06 on our pricing model.
[08:45] Maya Patel: Nice gap. How about answer quality delta?
[08:50] Marcus Ortiz: We compute token-level overlap and embedding-similarity for answers. On these prompts, overlap is about 0.86, and human preference leaning to Llama 3 for a couple of complex reasoning items.
[09:05] Dr. Priya Sharma: That's useful. For triage we'll want to prioritize latency but keep a fallback to Llama 3 for tricky cases. Is that easy?
[09:12] Elena Park: Yep — route initial quick answers to Mistral and if confidence is low or a follow-up is flagged, escalate to Llama 3 with a slight added latency.
[09:25] Rebecca Lin: Heading toward time — any blockers on our side for running a pilot?
[09:29] Jordan Lee: We need pricing for a pilot (est monthly) and the security docs. Also we'll want a short perf estimate for your Dedicated config.
[09:36] Rebecca Lin: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet and the benchmark/compatibility artifacts. Marcus will run a perf estimate for the Dedicated pool.
[09:42] Maya Patel: We'll also prepare a 100-prompt redacted set.
[09:46] Evan Kim: And I'll compile the compliance checklist.
[09:49] Rebecca Lin: Great, recap and next steps a bit later. Any other questions?
[09:53] Dr. Priya Sharma: One more — what's the typical time to onboard to Dedicated?
[09:57] Elena Park: Usually 2-4 weeks from contract signature — includes capacity provisioning and a short validation run. Private can take longer depending on networking.
[10:10] [10:10] Marcus Ortiz: Quick note: model compatibility for some older Falcon checkpoints requires a custom kernel; if you rely on that family we'll include a note in the matrix.
[10:20] Jordan Lee: Good to know.
[10:22] Rebecca Lin: Ok we'll capture all of this in the follow-up email with links.
[10:27] [10:27] (wrap-up)
[10:30] Rebecca Lin: Thanks everyone for your time. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet, compatibility matrix, security pack, initial pricing, and proposed pilot plan by Thursday.
[10:40] Dr. Priya Sharma: Thanks, looking forward to it.
[10:44] Marcus Ortiz: Thanks all.
[10:46] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and missing micro-numbers during the live perf demo; overall medium-quality automated transcription.
notes: AE+SE demo focused on model selection, benchmarks, and compatibility. Customer to provide redacted prompts; Redwood to provide benchmarking artifacts and security pack. Pilot aimed for early May.
